title: Console metric and trace coverage remediation after capacity event
creator: Carlos Mendes
description: Post-incident follow-up for a Dedicated capacity surge on 2026-02-23 that exposed multiple observability blind spots in the Redwood Console. During the event, key dashboards and alerts failed to surface per-model and per-route latency regressions and cache effectiveness; sampling and cardinality choices prevented tracing from linking latency spikes to a new kernel scheduler regression. This ticket tracks instrumentation gaps, dashboard fixes, alert tuning, tracing sampling rules, and follow-up verification steps.
comments: 2026-02-24 - Carlos M: Added initial incident summary and linked incident timeline. Noted that console alerts fired ~12 minutes after customer reports due to aggregated token-rate thresholds.

2026-02-26 - Priya N: Reproduced missing metric: kv_cache.hit_rate is present at host granularity but not emitted with model or tenant tags. Working on PR to add 'model' and 'tenant' tags to cache metrics.

2026-03-02 - Aisha Khan: UX review - existing latency dashboard aggregates across models and masks 95th percentile regressions for a handful of large-context models. Proposed new 'Per-model latency heatmap' panel and a top-N slow-routes table.

2026-03-05 - Ethan Liu: Tracing instrumentation note - current sampling policy uses uniform 1% sampling across routes. Will prototype adaptive sampling (error/high-latency biased) and a sampling rule for runtime-exec latency > 200ms.
2026-03-09 - Priya N: PRs open for metric tagging and dashboard changes. Need SRE review on alert thresholds and runbook updates before closing.
2026-03-10 - Carlos M: Prioritized items for next cycle. Marked security_review_required on KMS audit logs change (string flag set below).
